text:
alex: Heads up — noticed group-B of the A/B rollout (5%) spiked CPU at ~02:14 UTC after the recent batching/kernel selector change. Perf-bot flagged it. Anyone oncall?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-18T02:10Z started version v2.3.8-ab-batching (group B) - 5% traffic.

perf-bot: CI perf alert: staged-tests/latency-95 increased from ~120ms -> ~380ms on linux-gpu (trace id t-8e7).

maria: I see a strong correlation with merge 7f2c9d — it switched the kernel selector to prefer fused attention when batch shapes look 'long' and enabled more aggressive batch packing.

jen: Also KV miss rate jumped at the same time. KV cache TTL evictions are up ~4x. Looks like batch packing is creating many short-lived cache entries.

alex: Can we get a quick revert candidate? If it's causing production tail spikes we should pause.

sam: Running a bisect now across merges from last 24h. If perf-bot can run the microbench that reproduces tail-latency, it'll speed things up.

perf-bot: Started bisect job bisect/latency-tail/group-B against commits since 2026-03-17. Current candidate: 7f2c9d — local microbench reproduces ~x3 p95 regression.

maria: Confirmed repro locally with a 1k-prefix synthetic load: when selector picks fused kernel + aggressive packing p95 jumps ~3x.

jen: Profiler shows thread CPU dominated by kernel selection loop and a lot of time in cache compaction paths. The packing heuristic is producing many small batches that thrash the KV LRU and GC.

alex: Proposed mitigation: pause canary for group B (throttle to 0), and flip runtime selector fallback to legacy for affected routes: prefer_legacy_on_kv_churn=true.

sam: How quickly can we flip that? We have a runtime flag 'kernel.selector.memo' exposed via route overrides.

alex: Quick patch I can push to console to set a per-route override. Patch snippet:
```
POST /api/v1/routes/{route_id}/overrides
{
  "kernel_selector": {
    "prefer_legacy_on_kv_churn": "true",
    "batch_pack_threshold_ms": 5
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: Applied route override to /v1/generate for group B at 02:28Z (operator: alex). Canary paused.

perf-bot: Rerunning microbench after override... p95 now ~140ms — back within SLO. KV evictions decreased significantly.

maria: Good but we need a longer run. Can we add an automated SLO gate to pause rollouts if p95 > 2x baseline for a sustained window (eg 5–10m)?

jen: Agree. Proposed gate: if (p95 >= baseline * 2) for window 5m AND kv_eviction_rate >= baseline * 2 -> auto-pause + rollback to previous stable release. That combined signal reduces noisy alerts.

sam: Implementation note: add a canary-slo-checker job in the rollout pipeline that queries p95 from perf metrics and kv telemetry. We already have p95 alerts; extend checker to evaluate combined condition and call the rollout API to pause.

alex: Also add a CI microbench that simulates the small-batch packing + KV churn scenario to catch regressions pre-merge.

maria: Filed infra ticket infra/rollout-gates#412 to add the gate and the smoke microbench. I'll open the PR to wire the checker.

jen: For the bisect, mark 7f2c9d as culprit. We'll open a revert PR and follow with a targeted fix: change packing heuristic to avoid creating tiny batches when kv_eviction_rate is high, and add a guard in kernel selector to prefer legacy kernel when eviction rate spikes.

alex: Thanks team. I'll keep canary paused and monitor metrics for 1h. If green we'll resume with a slower ramp and the new gate. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Noted. Bisect result: culprit=7f2c9d, perf delta p95:+260ms. Generating revert PR template.

alex: I'll own the rollback PR and the route override until we get the selector fix in.

maria: I'll coordinate the gate PR and add the telemetry queries.

jen: Adding unit test for packing heuristic to the repo so future merges exercise the small-batch scenario.

sam: Nice quick turnaround. Keep me posted if the bisect or longer-run test disagrees. :eyes:
